tossups.text: Three "whiffles" and a "delta frame" composed primarily of beryllium are used to support one of these objects, also made from beryllium. The Caris Lab under the football stadium of the University of Arizona is the US's leading manufacturer of the largest type of these objects, which it manufactures from Ohara's E6 product using a custom-designed oven. Lightweight examples of these objects use a ribbed support that resembles a honeycomb. The LZT experiment uses an inexpensive type of these devices that consists of a rotating pool of liquid mercury. Guido d'Arturo pioneered a method for constructing large examples of these objects that results in a characteristic "six spike" diffraction pattern. Seven of these objects will span 25 meters to form a "Giant" structure named for Magellan. 18 hexagonal segments unfolded into a single primary one of these objects at L2 for the James Webb Space Telescope. For 10 points, name these structures that are used in reflecting telescopes.

The Planck (plonk) epoch immediately followed this event. Evidence for this event includes the CMBR and Hubble's law, which shows that galaxies are moving apart. Following this event, protons and neutrons fused to form atoms like deuterium and helium. For 10 points, name this event around 14 billion years ago in which the universe expanded from a single point.

this structure is essential for trachea structure. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in trachea structure.

tossups.text: The Breslovers sect inaugurated a tradition on this holiday of making a pilgrimage to the Ukrainian city of Uman, which, since 2020, has been a national holiday in Ukraine. An artist known as Haggai is best-known for the images and light verses he created for greeting cards or "Tovas" sent on this holiday. Some celebrants of this holiday throw bread into water to cast away past sins in a process called tashlich. This holiday begins a period sometimes called the 10 Days of Awe. It is common to eat apples dipped in honey on this holiday. A tekiah and three shevarim are blown on the shofar on this holiday. For 10 points, name this first of the High Holy Days in Judaism, which marks the Jewish New Year.

In 2008, a riot occurred in this country's capital over the murder of Ram Hari Shrestha by a faction of one of its political parties. It is currently led by prime minister Girija Korala, despite threat from Prachanda's ten-year Maoist insurgency and from Gyanendra, who was scheduled to lose his position as king in May 2008. For 10 points, name this country whose political crisis was exacerbated by a 2001 mass shooting by the crown prince at the royal palace, and which also faces a refugee crisis as citizens return from fellow Himalayan state Bhutan.

This novel's narrator remarks on the "sad gray, brown, or black" clothes of people in the marketplace in a chapter describing a public holiday. A mansion in this novel is compared to "Aladdin's palace" and contains a suit of gleaming armor which a girl points out to her mother. This novel concludes by describing a marking "on a field, sable" found on a shared grave in the yard of King's Chapel; the same place is the setting of its first chapter, which describes a rose-bush which grows outside a prison door. Three different scenes in this novel are set at a scaffold, such as one in which a preacher dies after giving a sermon on Election Day due to guilt over his affair with Roger Chillingworth's wife. For 10 points, name this novel about the adultery of Hester Prynne, written by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

A theory of this concept by John Lee is represented by a colour wheel and includes the term Ludus. Three components of this concept make up eight different types in its triangular theory by Robert Sternberg. In a book titled for its "Art," Erich Fromm wrote that this concept could be taught in a book. A book titled for the "Nature" of this concept included an experiment that used dolls made of cloth and wire as surrogate mothers and was written by Harry Harlow. Representing life, Sigmund Freud contrasted a Greek word for this concept with Thanatos to show two opposing drives within an individual's psyche. For 10 points, name this concept that the ancient Greeks subdivided into categories like eros.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on eros until mentioned with “What is the English term?”

tossups.text: A movement titled for this figure includes a slow section that was adapted for the hymn "Thaxted."Johann Salomon nicknamed a composer's forty-first symphony after this figure. In another work, a movement after "Mercury, the Winged Messenger" is named for a "Bringer of Jollity" with this name. For 10 points, give this shared name of Mozart's final symphony, a movement of Gustav Holst's The Planets, and the chief Roman god.

One of these conflicts saw the Fabian strategy to combat a general who had earlier won the battles of Trebia and Lake Trasimene. The first of these wars fought over the control of Sicily, and during the last of these wars the earth was salted. In one of these wars, Scipio Africanus triumphed at the battle of Zama over Hannibal, who had earlier won at Cannae. For 10 points, name this set of three wars between Carthage and Rome.

One artwork from this century in Volterra Cathedral shows brightly-dressed men on ladders assisting the Deposition of Christ, and is by Rosso Fiorentino. St Jerome holds a scroll in the corner of a painting from this century showing a large baby Jesus and a long-necked Madonna. An anamorphic skull lies below Jean de Dinteville in a work from this century. Most masterpieces by Parmigianino, a Mannerist artist, were made in this century. For 10 points, name this century in which Hans Holbein the Younger made many works for Henry VIII.

In one poem by this writer, the speaker says that the title idea "perches in the soul." In addition to "Hope is the thing with feathers," this author wrote a poem that proclaims "I'm Nobody! Who are you?" and a poem that describes a "blue, uncertain, stumbling buzz". A poem about a carriage ride with Death and Immortality was written by, for 10 points, what poet of "Because I could not stop for death," and "I heard a fly buzz when I died"?

As Lord Lieutenant of Ireland, this man put down the United Irishmen Rebellion and as Governor-General of India, he implemented Permanent Settlement. At the Battle of Long Island, this man, along with Sir Henry Clinton, led the advance guard that landed at Gravesend Bay. This man's most famous act was actually performed by a proxy, General Charles O'Hara, who surrendered to Benjamin Lincoln, the subordinate of George Washington. This general defeated Gen. Horatio Gates in the last major British victory in the south, the Battle of Camden. For 10 points, name this famous British general who is best known for his surrender at Yorktown.

While traveling with the charioteer Channa, this figure was shown the "four sights" of an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a monk. In a sermon at Deer Park, this figure revealed the Four Noble Truths. This former prince, who discovered the Eightfold Path, meditated under a bodhi tree to attain nirvana. For 10 points, name this enlightened figure, born Siddhartha Gautama, who founded a namesake Asian religion.

Description acceptable. Isaac Leeser and Isaac Wise debated this theory after discoveries in Newark, Ohio. Antonio de Montezinos alleged that proof of it led Menasseh ben Israel to proclaim that the Messiah would soon arrive. The "limited geography model" is an interpretation of this theory that is meant to explain the scant archeological evidence for it. Proponents of it in the 1840s believed the ruins of Quirigua in Guatemala were actually ruins of Zarahemla, a city founded by descendants of Zedekiah. The Church of Latter-Day Saints affirms this theory in its Articles of Faith, and origin story of the Nephites and Lamanites is a version of it. The discovery of phylacteries in Pittsfield, Massachusetts was promoted as evidence for this theory in the early 19th century. For 10 points, name this belief that people encountered by Europeans in the New World are distant relatives of the Jewish people.
acceptableAnswers: Native Americans are descendents of the Lost Tribes of Israel
prompt on answers like “the historicity of the Book of Mormon”
accept answers involving the Nephites and the Native Americans being equivalent
the Nephites going to North America

tossups.text: In a homoerotic Robert Duncan poem titled for this body part, the speaker's lover is compared to "the red-flowering eucalyptus, / the madrone, the yew." After picking up where a poem titled for this body part leaves off, Ocean Vuong supposes that the "body is more than / a portion of night" in a poem titled for one "of Air." The closing line of Osip Mandelstam's "Stalin Epigram" refers to the wideness of Stalin's "Ossetian" one of these body parts. One of these body parts "is still suffused with brilliance from inside, like a lamp" according to a poem titled for one that contains a "dark center where procreation flared." For 10 points, the admonition "You must change your life" ends a Rilke poem titled for what body part of an "archaic" Apollo statue?

An organization consisting of these people created the "Carville Star" program to disseminate research into leprosy. Harry Colmery allegedly jotted down the first draft of a legislation concerning these people on a napkin. These people benefitted from a so-called "club" in which they received 20 dollars a week for 52 weeks. The 85/15 rule capped funds for schools educating these people, leading to the creation of numerous "fly-by-night" colleges. Jim Webb championed a "post-9/11" legislation concerning these people, who were led by Walter Waters in a 1932 march on Washington, D.C. These people, who formed the American Legion, were the subject of the 1944 GI Bill. For 10 points, name these returning Americans who fought in the World Wars.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Bonus Army by asking “what people made up the Bonus Army?”

tossups.text: The Royal Feast of the Sun was observed at a mach'ay cave at this location located north of the Condor Stone. An archaeologist discovered this location while searching for the lost city of Vilcabamba (VEEL-kah-BAHM-bah). At this site, the Temple of the Three Windows is located near the "The Hitching Post of the Sun," Intihuatana (IN-tee-wah-TAH-nah). This site, which may have been an estate for Pachacuti (PAH-chah-KOO-tee), was rediscovered by Hiram Bingham. For 10 points, name this citadel north of Cuzco in the Andes that was built by the Incan Empire.

Two values of this quantity are found at the intersection of the bubble point and dew point curves in a binary mixture diagram. The ratio of the change in enthalpy and this quantity often equals between 85 and 88 joules per mole Kelvin according to Trouton's Rule. Due to having different values for this quantity compared to its substituents, azeotropes are unable to be separated by distillation. Adding solute to a pure solvent can increase this quantity in its namesake elevation. The vapor pressure equals the external pressure at this point. For 10 points, name this quantity, the temperature at which a liquid transitions into a gas.

A film blends shots of one of these structures together as the narrator quotes Falstaff's metaphor about "naked, poor, forked radish" in discussion of "this grand choiring shot of affirmation." In a 1963 film, the camera pans up to show one of these structures as a man asks, "who put that there?" right after his suit is ruined by ice cream spilled by Audrey Hepburn's character. Narration over a montage depicting one of these structures argues that artworks eventually overshadow their creators' identity; that scene is from Orson Welles's F for Fake. A Canadian tourist's suicidal jump off of this sort of structure results in the death of Amélie's mother. In Before Sunset, Jesse and Celine discuss how one of these structures "will be gone one day" as they sight-see along the Seine. For 10 points, what sort of structure names a Disney film about Quasimodo?

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for gallbladder and bile. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in gallbladder and bile.
